key_insight: CausalCine enables real-time, autoregressive generation of multi-shot video narratives by explicitly modeling shot boundaries, viewpoint shifts, and event progression so long rollouts remain dynamic and semantically coherent.
problem_solved: Existing autoregressive video models treat long sequences as extended single shots and therefore suffer from motion stagnation and semantic drift during long rollouts; this work addresses coherent, multi-shot cinematic storytelling in real time.
method: Shot-aware causal autoregressive architecture that explicitly represents and conditions on shot boundaries and viewpoint changes.
Event/scene progression mechanisms (state resets or hierarchical conditioning) to prevent motion stagnation and semantic drift over long rollouts.
Training and inference strategies optimized for low-latency, real-time generation of open-ended multi-shot narratives.
impact: Enables practitioners to generate longer, cinematic video sequences that maintain motion diversity and semantic consistency in real time—useful for content creation, interactive storytelling, and VFX pipelines.
visual_elements: Timeline diagram showing multiple shots with explicit shot-boundary markers and viewpoint-change arrows
Before vs after comparison: long-rollout single-shot model (stagnant/blurred) vs CausalCine (dynamic/coherent)

Chart showing quality/consistency vs rollout length comparing baseline autoregressive models and CausalCine
paper_title: CausalCine: Real-Time Autoregressive Generation for Multi-Shot Video Narratives
paper_authors: Yihao Meng, Zichen Liu, Hao Ouyang, Qiuyu Wang, Ka Leong Cheng
